profile.reading: QTS Richmond 2 (RIC2) is a data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, just east of Richmond and immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport, developed by QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services, renamed following the company's 2013 IPO; this registry tracks both names as the same operator). Per QTS's own site, the campus spans approximately 85 acres and is planned to include five buildings once fully built out, with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon completion; that figure describes the campus as a whole rather than any single building, and much of it was not yet in operation as of the source page, so it is not applied here as this building's own confirmed capacity. This building, DC1, sits at 6030 Technology Boulevard, one of five addressed buildings running along Technology Boulevard: 6030 (DC1), 6040 (DC2), 6050 (DC3), 6060 (DC5), and 6070 (DC6); the campus's own numbering skips DC4 entirely, a naming gap this registry notes rather than attempts to explain. RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond-area campus, distinct from the company's original Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus elsewhere in the metro, which this registry documents as a separate set of facilities. Henrico County, where Sandston sits, has become one of the mid-Atlantic's fastest-growing data center corridors in recent years, drawing hyperscale and colocation development on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and dense regional fiber routes running through the Richmond area. QTS's own campus page does not state which, if any, of the five RIC2 buildings are currently operating versus still under construction, and does not publish individual square footage, IT capacity, or year-opened figures for any single building on the campus; none of those figures is asserted here for DC1 specifically, consistent with this registry's practice of reporting only what the operator has actually confirmed at the building level.

reading.body:
QTS Richmond 2 is a planned 180 megawatt data center campus spanning approximately 85 acres in Sandston, Virginia, near Richmond International Airport. The campus will eventually comprise five buildings when fully built out, of which this entry describes DC1 at 6030 Technology Boulevard; QTS's published materials do not specify which of the five buildings are currently operating, their individual capacities, or when DC1 specifically came online. No individual building-level IT power figure is available from the operator for DC1.

At the planned campus capacity of 180 MW and assuming industry-standard densities, this represents roughly 4,500 racks under typical colocation density or 1,800 racks under high-density AI training assumptions; this campus, once complete, would rank among mid-Atlantic hyperscale sites by scale. Virginia published capacity totals 1,375 megawatts across 23 facilities with disclosed figures; the RIC2 campus's 180 MW planned capacity would represent approximately 13 percent of the state's published data center power if fully realized, though this figure describes a future state and assumes completion as planned.

Henrico County, where this site sits, has emerged as a major mid-Atlantic data center corridor on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and regional fiber infrastructure. The campus ranks 24th nationally among published facilities by planned capacity, but this ranking reflects a future state; Virginia's actual grid constraint and the timing of RIC2's buildout completion remain unpublished variables for assessing when this capacity will materially affect AI infrastructure availability.
